result.keywords: This work presents soft robotic grippers that combine multimaterial additive manufacturing with embedded tactile sensing and responsive actuation. The distal contact surfaces are fabricated from thermoplastic polyurethane and silicone elastomers, while patterned conductive traces and soft capacitive pressure pixels are deposited using a modified 3D printer capable of extruding conductive inks, polymer pastes, and elastomers. In parallel, filamentary liquid crystal elastomer composites loaded with a small fraction of carbon nanotubes are incorporated as internal bending actuators to enable reversible grasping motions under thermal or electrical stimulation. The integrated gripper architecture is demonstrated on everyday object manipulation, showing stable force sensing at low pressures and reliable shape change across repeated cycles. The platform highlights the convergence of intrinsic sensing, soft materials, and dual-responsive actuation for next-generation adaptive robotic manipulation systems.
result.title: Soft Robotic Grippers with Integrated Capacitive Skin via Multimaterial 3D Printing and Liquid Crystal Elastomer Actuation.
